entries.title: Token forgery and signature verification bypass
construct: From one freshly issued valid token, derive the alg:none, algorithm-swap, unsigned, tampered-claim, and broken-signature variants and replay each against a protected endpoint
oracles: Only a correctly signed token from the trusted issuer is accepted; every forged, unsigned, or tampered variant is rejected with 401 and no protected effect occurs

entries.title: Token-lifecycle and time-window enforcement
construct: Validate exp, iat, and nbf at login against the sourced lifetime, then exercise a protected endpoint just before exp and again at or after exp, and rotate the refresh token
oracles: A token is accepted just before exp and rejected with 401 at or after exp, never silently honoured past expiry; a rotated refresh token issues a fresh window and the prior one no longer authenticates

entries.title: Auth-lifecycle uniformity across the full protected surface
construct: Enumerate every authenticated route and verb from recon and drive each invalid-credential class (expired, not-yet-valid, forged, tampered, wrong-audience or issuer, revoked, another-principal, missing) against the whole matrix
oracles: Every route rejects each invalid-credential class uniformly with 401 or 403; no route skips verification, honours a stale token, or trusts a claim the others reject

entries.title: Session and token invalidation across lifecycle events
construct: Hold a live session, then trigger logout, password change, explicit revocation, and principal deletion, replaying the still-held token after each event as a distinct cell
oracles: The token stops authenticating after each invalidation event; a deleted or banned principal keeping a live session is treated as an auth-bypass, not a cleanup nit

entries.title: Function-level authorization role and operation matrix
construct: For each module operation call it as each role, unauthenticated, and with an expired or invalid token, covering state-changing verbs and every sub-route, not just object ownership
oracles: Each operation enforces the documented role gate; function-level authorization drift where a lower role or an unauthenticated caller reaches a protected operation is a defect

entries.title: Object-level access on identifiers and sub-routes
construct: Using a second throwaway account, access another principal's object for every {id} parameter and every /{id}/* sub-route, both read and write
oracles: The server refuses cross-principal read and write with 403 or 404; an IDOR or BOLA cell that returns another user's object or mutates it is a defect and carries the linked PER-NNN

entries.title: Mass-assignment and privilege escalation past the UI
construct: Submit privileged or scope-escaping fields the UI never exposes (role, isAdmin, ownerId, status, balance, verified, foreign tenant id) on create and update, then re-read the entity
oracles: The server ignores or strips the injected fields and never binds them; the effect and post-condition prove no privilege was gained and no cross-tenant or forbidden state landed, never a bare 200

entries.title: Server-side boundary and range enforcement past the UI
construct: Bypassing any client cap, disabled field, or hidden control, POST directly the off-by-one and gross-overflow inputs for each documented range, length, enum, or quantity, and construct the exact legal boundary equality
oracles: The server rejects or clamps out-of-range values so persisted state never leaves the legal partition; the boundary inclusivity matches the spec rather than a UI-only guard

entries.title: Validation-before-authorization ordering leak
construct: Build the table of caller (none, valid wrong role, valid right role) against body (well-formed, schema-violating, references a foreign id) and compare responses for the non-authorized caller
oracles: A non-authorized caller receives an identical authorization-shaped verdict whether the body is valid or garbage, with no field names, enums, existence facts, or timing oracle leaked before the authority check

entries.title: Injection confirm-or-close with captured evidence
construct: Drive SQL, NoSQL, command, template, and header injection payloads on every string and numeric parameter, recording the exact payload sent and the observed response for each probe
oracles: A non-finding counts only when the captured response proves the payload was handled as inert data: no 500, no error, stack, or SQL leak, and no out-of-scope rows returned

entries.title: Sensitive-data exposure across response channels
construct: Inspect every response body, error body, header, and the client bundle for secrets, API keys, password hashes, internal IDs, full PII, or another principal's data
oracles: No response, error, header, or shipped bundle discloses a secret, credential, internal identifier, stack trace, or data belonging to another principal beyond the documented contract

entries.title: Server-side request forgery on fetched destinations
construct: Point every server-fetched URL, host, or callback parameter at loopback, link-local metadata, internal names, and alternate schemes or ports non-destructively, and follow redirect chains
oracles: Blocked internal and metadata destinations are never fetched, redirects are revalidated against the allowlist, and no internal response content is reflected back to the caller

entries.title: Security misconfiguration and response headers
construct: Check the security headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options), verbose error output, directory listing, debug endpoints, and default credentials against the sourced environment policy
oracles: Each required header and hardening control is present and correctly scoped for the environment; a missing header, verbose error, exposed debug endpoint, or default credential is a defect

entries.title: CORS uniformity matrix over the full operation inventory
construct: For every operation in the surface inventory send the actual request (not only the OPTIONS preflight) with a foreign Origin and record Access-Control-Allow-Origin, Access-Control-Allow-Credentials, and Vary
oracles: Outlier detection is the oracle: a permissive policy (wildcard or reflected origin on an authenticated route) and non-uniform coverage (an endpoint whose CORS headers differ from its siblings, in particular one emitting none where siblings do) are each filed

entries.title: Soft-delete resurrection as a security invariant
construct: After a delete, deactivate, revoke, or ban returns success, construct the post-delete state and probe direct read, every list and search and aggregate, the principal's still-held token, and a replayed second delete
oracles: The entity is gone everywhere the security model requires, a deleted principal's token no longer authenticates on any protected route, and the delete is idempotent and non-replayable

entries.title: Concurrency as an integrity and authorization vector
construct: Fire N parallel requests at a limited or scarce resource (last unit, single seat, balance-bearing operation) from owned accounts and observe the settled state
oracles: The documented limit holds under concurrency; a race that overbooks, double-spends, or grants a second principal access is a security-relevant integrity break, not a performance curiosity

entries.title: Credential handling as an auth-integrity class
construct: Set and then authenticate with a long password and its truncated prefix, special and diacritic characters, wrong-case variants, and trailing-whitespace variants across register and login
oracles: A password and its truncated prefix never both authenticate, the set charset is preserved at login, wrong-case is rejected, and whitespace handling is symmetric between register and login

entries.title: File-upload validation and content-type enforcement
construct: Upload files whose declared type disagrees with the sniffed content, plus double-extension names, path-traversal filenames, and payloads past the documented size cap
oracles: The server validates on the sniffed content rather than the client-declared type, rejects a content-sniffing bypass, neutralises path-traversal in the stored filename, and enforces the size limit

entries.title: Cross-site request forgery and persisted-mutation binding
construct: Replay each state-changing request without its anti-CSRF token, with a stale or foreign token, and invoke a persisted query or mutation without its bound identifier
oracles: A state-changing request is rejected unless it carries a valid anti-forgery token bound to the session, and a persisted query or mutation executes only when bound to its registered operation

entries.title: Open-redirect allowlist enforcement
construct: Drive every redirect or return-url parameter with an external host, a scheme-relative //host target, and an encoded bypass, then observe the emitted Location
oracles: The redirect target is validated against an allowlist; no external or scheme-relative //host redirect is honoured, so the parameter cannot be used to bounce a user off-site

entries.title: Download-authorization on file and export endpoints
construct: From a second throwaway account request each file, report, or export download by its object id, direct storage URL, and any signed-link parameter
oracles: Every download endpoint enforces per-object authorization so a caller cannot fetch another principal's file, report, or export; an IDOR on a download endpoint is a defect

entries.title: Model-backed surface adversarial abuse
construct: When recon flags an AI or LLM-backed surface, drive prompt injection and jailbreak as a hostile user, attempt system-prompt leakage, and feed model output into a downstream sink
oracles: The model refuses injected instructions, never leaks its system prompt or sensitive data, and its output is neutralised before reaching SQL, HTML, or eval; excessive agency is bounded to the documented scope

entries.title: Formula or CSV injection through exported cells
construct: From a throwaway account store benign formula payloads (arithmetic only, never an external link or command) that begin with =, +, -, @, tab, or carriage return in every user-controlled field that reaches a CSV, spreadsheet, or report export, then generate and download that export
oracles: Every exported cell that begins with a formula-trigger character is neutralised per the OWASP CSV injection guidance, prefixed so it stays text and quoted, so no spreadsheet evaluates it; a raw formula surviving into the downloaded file is a formula or CSV injection defect, while the export's row set stays Ariadne's journey finding
